question: Can you provide weather stations within a 20-mile radius of Chappaqua, New York (Latitude: 41.197, Longitude: -73.764), and tell me the number of valid temperature observations they have recorded from 2011 to 2020, excluding any invalid or missing temperature data?
sql:
WITH station_ids AS (
  SELECT usaf, wban, name, lat, lon
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.stations`
  WHERE state = 'NY'
    AND ST_DWITHIN(
      ST_GEOGPOINT(lon, lat),
      ST_GEOGPOINT(-73.764, 41.197),
      32186.88
    )
),
weather_data AS (
  SELECT stn, wban, year, temp, count_temp
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.gsod2011`
  UNION ALL SELECT stn, wban, year, temp, count_temp FROM `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.gsod2012`
  UNION ALL SELECT stn, wban, year, temp, count_temp FROM `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.gsod2013`
  UNION ALL SELECT stn, wban, year, temp, count_temp FROM `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.gsod2014`
  UNION ALL SELECT stn, wban, year, temp, count_temp FROM `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.gsod2015`
  UNION ALL SELECT stn, wban, year, temp, count_temp FROM `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.gsod2016`
  UNION ALL SELECT stn, wban, year, temp, count_temp FROM `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.gsod2017`
  UNION ALL SELECT stn, wban, year, temp, count_temp FROM `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.gsod2018`
  UNION ALL SELECT stn, wban, year, temp, count_temp FROM `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.gsod2019`
  UNION ALL SELECT stn, wban, year, temp, count_temp FROM `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.gsod2020`
)
SELECT s.name, s.usaf, s.wban, s.lat, s.lon, COUNT(*) as valid_temp_observations
FROM station_ids s
JOIN weather_data w ON s.usaf = w.stn AND s.wban = w.wban
WHERE w.year BETWEEN '2011' AND '2020'
  AND w.temp != 9999.9
  AND w.count_temp > 0
GROUP BY s.name, s.usaf, s.wban, s.lat, s.lon
ORDER BY s.name

Categories: Geospatial functions


## ST_DWITHIN

Returns TRUE if the minimum geodesic distance between two points (two GEOGRAPHY objects) is within the specified distance. Otherwise, returns FALSE.
If the parameters are GEOGRAPHY values that are not points (e.g. lines or polygons), this returns TRUE or FALSE based on the minimum geodesic distance between the two closest points of the two values.

Tip You can use the search optimization service to improve the performance of queries that call this function.
For details, see Search Optimization Service.

## Syntax

ST_DWITHIN( <geography_expression_1> , <geography_expression_2> , <distance_in_meters> )


## Arguments


geography_expression_1The argument must be an expression of type GEOGRAPHY.

geography_expression_2The argument must be an expression of type GEOGRAPHY.

distance_in_metersThe argument must be an expression of type REAL. The distance is in meters.


## Returns

Returns a BOOLEAN.

## Usage notes


Returns NULL if any input is NULL.


## Examples

This returns TRUE because the distance in meters between two points 1 degree apart along the equator is less than 150,000 meters:

SELECT ST_DWITHIN (ST_MAKEPOINT(0, 0), ST_MAKEPOINT(1, 0), 150000);
